series.name: The Unseated Series
series.about: Confronting the systems, mindsets, and patterns that prevent maturity and limit Kingdom impact. Whatever has taken God's seat must be unseated.

context.name: Context Matters
context.about: The verses we quote most confidently are often the ones we understand least. Every episode returns one passage to its original weight: who wrote it, why, what the words meant, then what it asks of us today.

episodes.title: When Ministry Outpaces Maturity
episodes.hook: What happens when someone carries a genuine gift but an unformed character?
summary: You can be gifted and still immature. What happens when ministry grows faster than the person carrying it?

Season One opens by confronting what happens when gifting, visibility, and ministry activity outpace spiritual formation. Using 1 Corinthians 13:1–3, we examine how performance can quietly replace formation, why spiritual gifts are not evidence of spiritual maturity, and what happens when leaders learn how to function publicly before they have submitted to God's refining work privately.
This conversation is not an attack on gifting, excellence, or effective ministry. It is a call back to submission, maturity, obedience, and dependence on the Holy Spirit.

episodes.title: The Drug Called Power
episodes.hook: What happens when we become more impressed by the manifestation of power than we are committed to being formed by God?
summary: Acts 8 and Simon the Sorcerer expose a danger the modern church still faces: craving spiritual power, signs, encounters, and influence without deeper submission to Christ.

Simon amazed an entire community. People associated him with greatness. But when the Gospel arrived, Luke reveals that fascination with power and genuine spiritual formation are not the same thing. The issue was never simply what Simon could do. The deeper question was who he was submitted to.

The modern church knows how to create powerful moments. We know how to generate momentum and move rooms. But noise is not glory. Response is not fruit. Encounters reveal God's power, but encounters alone do not mature the heart. Formation does. Refining does. Obedience does.
God is not calling us back to stronger encounters at the expense of formation. He is calling us back to deeper submission. And that is where true power has always lived.

episodes.title: When Glory Goes Missing
episodes.hook: What does 1 Samuel 4 teach us about a church that can remain active while drifting out of alignment with God?
summary: Israel still had the Ark. The priests were still in position. The people still knew how to shout. The earth even shook. But outward spiritual intensity was not the same as inward alignment.

This episode examines Israel's defeat in 1 Samuel 4, the capture of the Ark of the Covenant, the fall of Eli's house, and the naming of Ichabod: "The glory has departed." It explores the uncomfortable possibility that a religious system can preserve its structure, language, expressions, and experiences while losing the relationship that gave those things their weight.

This is not an argument against Pentecostal expression, spiritual gifts, structure, emotion, or powerful worship experiences. The question is deeper: what is our expression rooted in? Scripture shows us that intensity is not the final metric. Fruit is.

Once glory is gone, survival is not success. But the story does not end with Ichabod. There is still an invitation to come out of performance, return to alignment, and recover the weight of obedience, covenant, holiness, and consecration.

episodes.title: Romans 4:17 Does NOT Say What You Think It Says
episodes.quote: Call those things that be not as though they were
episodes.hook: This verse is quoted in churches every week with full confidence. But the context tells a completely different story.
summary: For years, "calling those things that are not as though they were" has been used to teach believers to declare healing, financial breakthrough, jobs, and desired outcomes into existence. But is that what Paul was actually saying?
In this episode we return Romans 4:17 to its context and examine what Paul is actually teaching about Abraham, faith, God's promise, and the One who truly calls things into existence.
Abraham's faith was not in the power of his own words. God spoke. Abraham believed. God fulfilled. The weight was never on Abraham's declaration. It was on God's character.

episodes.title: Psalm 37:4 Explained: Does God Really Give You What You Want?
episodes.hook: Does Psalm 37:4 mean God promises to give us whatever we want if we pray, fast, serve, and remain faithful?
summary: For many believers, Psalm 37:4 has been presented almost like a spiritual transaction: pray more, fast more, serve more, delight in God more, and eventually the blessing will follow.

But Psalm 37 was not written to people trying to acquire more. David was speaking as an older man to faithful people watching the wicked prosper while they suffered. His instruction was not to manipulate God into changing their circumstances, but to trust, dwell, delight, commit, rest, and wait on Him.

The promise is not simply that God fulfills the wish list you brought to Him. As God becomes your delight, He begins transforming the heart that wrote the list. This is the difference between transaction and transformation.

For those who have prayed, believed, served, and still wondered why God did not give them the outcome they expected: God has not failed you. Bad theology may have failed you. A mishandled verse may have failed you. But God has not moved.
